καυχώμενο ἐν ταῖ θλίψε ι καὶ εἰδὼ ὅτι ἡ θλίψι ὑπομονὴν κατεργάζεται καὶ
ὑπομένων. διὰ ταῦτα δὲ ἄξιον ἦν αὐτὸν ἀφορισθῆναι εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ
προγινωσκόμενον ἔσεσθαι, καὶ ἀφορισθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ. καὶ
ἀφωρίζετο εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ οὐ διὰ τὴν φύσιν ἔχουσάν τι ἐξαίρετον καὶ ὅσον ἐπὶ
τῇ κατασκευῇ ὑπὲρ τὰς τῶν μὴ τοιούτων φύσεις, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὰς προεγνωσμένας μὲν
πρότερον πράξεις ὕστερον δὲ γενομένας ἑκάστην ἐκ τῆς παρασκευῆς καὶ τῆς
προαιρέσεως τῆς ἀποστολικῆς. νῦν δὲ ἀποδιδόναι εἰς τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ ψαλμοῦ ῥητὸν οὐκ
ἦν εὔκαιρον, παρεκβατικὸν γὰρ ἦν· διὸ εἰς τὴν οἰκείαν τάξιν θεοῦ διδόντος
ἀποδοθήσεται, ὅταν τὸν ψαλμὸν διηγώμεθα. ἀρκέσει δὲ καὶ ταῦτα πεπλεονασμένα
εἰς τὸ ἀφωρισμένος. 2 i 9–11 μάρτυς γάρ μου ἐστὶν ὁ θεὸς ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί
μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι
πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου δεόμενος εἴπως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ
θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς. ἔστι δὲ καὶ χωρὶς
θελήματος θεοῦ ἥκειν πρός τινα, ὥσπερ ὁ Βαλαὰμ ἀπῄει πρὸς τὸν Βαλὰκ
καταρασόμενος μισθοῦ τὸν Ἰσραήλ· οἶμαι δὲ ὅτι καὶ πᾶς ἐθνικός, ἢ ὁπώσποτε τῆς
θεοσεβείας ἀλλότριος, μὴ διακονούμενος ἁγίοις τῶν λυσιτελῶν τι αὐτοῖς, οὐ καὶ ἐν
θελήματι θεοῦ εὐοδοῦται γίνεσθαι πρὸς οὓς γίνεται, εἰ καὶ εὐοδοῦταί ποτε· ἐ τὶ γὰρ
φησὶν ἡ γραφὴ ἐν κακοῖ εὐοδία ἀνδρό . 3 11, 12 ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν
πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς· τοῦτο δέ ἐστι συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ
τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ. ὡς ὄντος δὲ χαρίσματος μὴ πνευματικοῦ
ἡγοῦμαι ὅτι ἀναγκαίως πρόσκειται· ἔστι γάρ τινα χαρίσματα, οὐ πνευματικά, ὡς καὶ
ὁ γάμος· τὸ γὰρ πνευματικὸν οὐκ ἄν ποτε ἐμποδίσαι προ ευχῇ· ἡ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ
σύνοδος ἀνδρὸς καὶ γυναικὸς κωλύει. ὅτι δὲ χάρισμα ὁ γάμος δηλοῖ ὁ ἀπόστολος
φήσας θέλω πάντα ἀνθρώπου εἶναι ὡ καὶ ἐμαυτόν, ἀλλ' ἕκα το ἴδιον ἔχει χάρι μα
ἐκ θεοῦ· ὃ μὲν οὕτω , ὃ δὲ οὕτω . 4 i 13–15 οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι
πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ
καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν, Ἕλλησί τε καὶ
βαρβάροις· σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί, οὕτως τὸ κατ' ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ
ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι. [ἔστιν δὲ ἐνταῦθα καθ' ὑπερβατόν, ὃ ἐὰν μὴ
τηρηθῇ μάχεται τῇ ἀκολουθίᾳ· τίς γὰρ ἂν εἴποι διὰ τοῦτο κεκωλύσθαι ἐλθεῖν πρὸς
τοὺς Ῥωμαίους τὸν Παῦλον ἵνα καρπὸν ἔχῃς; τοὐναντίον γάρ, εἰ μὴ ἐκωλύθη
καρπὸν εἶχεν, κωλυόμενος δὲ ἀπεστερεῖτο τοῦ καρποῦ· πῶς οὖν ἀναγνωστέον;

θεοῦ ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν

ἡμαρτημένοις πόνων καὶ οἱ ὑπ' αὐτὸν τῶν αὐτῶν ὑπηρέται καὶ λειτουργοί, ὡς ὅτε

pass_a_gloss: Boasting in tribulation and knowing that tribulation produces endurance and endurance, therefore it was fitting for him to be set apart for the gospel of God, foreknown to come into being, and to be set apart from his mother's womb. He was set apart for the gospel of God not because of a nature possessing something extraordinary, nor on account of the construction above other natures, but because of foreknown earlier deeds and later actions arising from preparation and the apostolic choice. Now it was not timely to give what is stated in the psalm, for it was digressive; therefore, in the divine order God gives, it will be rendered when we recount the psalm. This will suffice even with excess for the one who is set apart. 2 i 9–11 For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that I continually make mention of you in my prayers, asking that by some means I may now at last succeed in coming to you by God's will; for I long to see you. And there is also coming to someone apart from God's will, just as Balaam went to Balak, cursing for hire against Israel; I think also that every Gentile, or whenever the worship of God is alien, not serving the holy things of benefit to them, does not prosper in God's will to become toward those toward whom they come, even if they prosper at times; for what does the scripture say in evil prosperity of man? 3 11, 12 That I may impart to you some spiritual gift to establish you; this is indeed to be mutually comforted among you by the faith which is in each other, yours and mine. As for the gift not being spiritual, I think it necessarily follows; for there are gifts, not spiritual, such as marriage; for the spiritual cannot ever be hindered by prayer; but the gathering of man and woman hinders it. That the apostle indicates marriage as a gift by saying I wish all men to be as I am, yet each has his own gift from God; one in this way, the other in that way. 4 i 13–15 I do not wish you to be ignorant, brothers, that I often planned to come to you and was hindered until now, that I might have some fruit among you, just as I also have among the other nations, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, I am a debtor, so that my eagerness and you in Rome may preach the gospel. [But here is a parenthetical remark, which if not observed contradicts the sequence; for who would say because of this Paul was hindered from coming to the Romans that he might have fruit? On the contrary, if he had not been hindered, he would have had fruit; but being hindered, he was deprived of the fruit; how then should we read? Often I planned to come to you that I might have some fruit among you, just as I also have among the other nations, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, and I was hindered until now; therefore why was the parenthetical inserted? Because the purpose clause 'that I may have some fruit' was about to connect with much (for example, 'that I also have among the other nations, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, I am a debtor, and the following') so that it would not break the continuity, having inserted 'I was hindered until now' he joined it to the former 'I planned to come to you' the 'that I may have some fruit', and thus he restored the order of the discourse.] 5 i 18 For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and injustice of people who suppress the truth in injustice. But then, those who labors through sins; thus I hear according to the allotment and unrepentant heart he stirs up anger in himself on the day of wrath, and the fact that he has reached yet his anger to the end. pass_b_english: Boasting in trials and recognizing that trials forge endurance, and endurance—because of this, it was proper for him to be designated for God’s gospel, foreknown to exist and to be set apart from his mother’s womb. He was appointed to the gospel of God not due to any exceptional nature, nor because of superiority over other natures, but because of previously known deeds and later actions born of preparation and apostolic choice. At present, it was not fitting to deliver what is written in the psalm, for it would be digressive; thus, in the divine ordering, it will be given when we recount the psalm—this will be sufficient, even in excess, for the one who is set apart. For God is my witness, whom I serve in spirit through the gospel of his Son, as I continually remember you in my prayers, asking that I might at last come to you by God’s will, for I long to see you. Indeed, someone may come not according to God’s will, just as Balaam went to Balak, cursing Israel for hire; I also believe that every Gentile, or whenever the worship of God is foreign, not ministering to the beneficial holy things for them, does not prosper in God’s purpose to become toward those they approach, even if they thrive temporarily—what does scripture say about the evil prosperity of man? That I may impart to you a spiritual gift to establish you; this is indeed mutual encouragement among you through the faith you share, yours and mine. Regarding a gift that is not spiritual, I consider it necessarily follows: there are non-spiritual gifts, such as marriage, for the spiritual gift can never be hindered by prayer, yet the union of man and woman impedes it. The apostle indicates marriage as a gift when he says, ‘I wish all people were as I am,’ yet each has his own gift from God—one in this manner, another in that. I do not wish you to be unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you and was hindered until now, so that I might bear fruit among you, just as I have among other nations—Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish—and I am a debtor, so that my eagerness and you in Rome may preach the gospel. [But here is a parenthetical remark, which, if ignored, disrupts the sequence; for who would claim Paul was hindered from coming to the Romans in order to bear fruit? On the contrary, if he had not been hindered, he would have borne fruit; but being hindered, he was deprived of it—how then should we read? Often I planned to come to you that I might bear fruit among you, just as I have among other nations, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, and I was hindered until now; therefore, why was the parenthetical inserted? Because the purpose clause ‘that I may bear fruit’ was about to connect with much—for example, ‘that I also bear fruit among the other nations, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, I am a debtor, and the following’—so that it would not break continuity. Having inserted ‘I was hindered until now,’ he joined it to the former ‘I planned to come to you’ and the ‘that I may bear fruit,’ thus restoring the discourse’s order.] For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and injustice of people who suppress the truth in injustice. It also seems to be spoken of as wrath and the servant of those who have sinned laboring, and those under him of the same servants and ministers, as when God’s wrath was set to burn in Israel, when he caused David to rise against them, he commanded Joab to number the people; but the second stands from having sent out their wrath, anger, and tribulation, vengeance through evil angels. But then, those who labor through sin—I hear according to the allotment and unrepentant heart, he stirs up anger within himself on the day of wrath, and the fact that he has reached yet his anger to the end. Regarding these matters, consider whether the things happening to the righteous, when the evil one tempts them, wrath is indeed not from God nor from heaven, but from below somewhere, or from the devil or some of his angels; yet for these, no one plausibly argues that we are to wage war before the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places, for these things will appear as those who are angry tearing apart the holy ones and bringing upon them wrath from heaven. choices.issue: Whether the wrath described in Romans 1:18 is directly from God or mediated through evil forces
choices.choice: The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against ungodliness, but when it manifests in human experience—especially in the suffering of the righteous under temptation—it may originate not from God directly, but from the devil or evil angels, as God permits or withdraws protection.

choices.issue: How Paul’s hindered journey to Rome relates to his desire to bear fruit among the believers
choices.choice: Paul’s repeated plans to visit Rome were hindered not to prevent fruitfulness, but to preserve the logical flow of his argument; the parenthetical clause was inserted to avoid a broken sequence, showing that hindrance deprived him of fruit, not that hindrance was the means to it.
